皮克斯终于也拍王子公主的故事了！谁都知道这是迪士尼的招牌菜！作为皮克斯的脑残粉，真不知道这是堕落的开始还是创新的尝试！美国各大电影公司都追求多样化的电影风格，你很难说什么是华纳电影的风格，什么是派拉蒙电影的风格，什么是20世纪福克斯电影的风格，唯独迪士尼电影可以成为一个名词解释，他们一定是欢乐温情的，人生观价值观绝对是主流的、积极向上的，常常出现可以媲美宝莱坞的华丽歌舞秀，不少电影都有发展成主题游乐园的潜力。而迪士尼的动画电影，从上世纪30年代的《白雪公主和七个小矮人》开始，王子和公主从此幸福的生活在一起的童话改编套路从没断过，最大的区别就是你叫白雪公主还是睡美人，叫小美人鱼还是长发公主？皮克斯和迪士尼联姻，但始终保持着相对独立性，《勇敢传说》之前，皮克斯的12部动画长片，坚持不要歌舞、故事原创不改编经典童话的原则，以区别于迪士尼的童话改编电影，所以皮克斯从没出现王子与公主的童话。这一次的《勇敢传说》，皮克斯用第一次以女性角色为主人公、第一部魔幻电影为宣传口号，以示创新，但这公主王子什么的，还是让我有点担心，尤其是《赛车总动员2》票房口碑双双落马还历历在目，皮克斯会不会一步一步丢失自己的特色，变得迪士尼化？因此《勇敢传说》中的梅莉达就显得非常独特，她一头浓烈的红发，红色常常象征热情，之于她就是对生活的热情，红发在影片中还代表了梅莉达的自我意识，当艾莉诺皇后帮梅莉达梳妆打扮准备迎接各部落首领的长子（王子男人）时，梅莉达的红发完全被衣服包裹，象征传统要束缚她的自我，去迎合男人的眼光，可她偏要让一缕红发露出来，又象征她对传统的反抗。如果说事业和爱情是当代女性的一个两难选择，那梅莉达在事业和爱情之间最终选择了自我，对国家（可以理解成事业），她承担起自己的责任，号召各部落团结起来，相亲相爱；对爱情，她不盲目，不幻想爱情但依然相信爱情，爱别人之前先学会爱自己，这完全是一个现代女孩的人生态度。而她的这种态度也影响了象征传统女性的艾莉诺皇后，皇后有着传统女性的诸多美德，温柔贤淑、优雅端庄、关键时刻还镇得住场面；可也因为传统的束缚常常失去自我，她的世界永远以丈夫和丈夫的事业为核心，并且把这种观点强加在女儿身上。然而当她变成一头熊，就能以另一种身份来审视这种生活，离开城堡，她的温柔、她的优雅在森林完全没有用武之地，而梅莉达却如鱼得水，因此她摘下了象征高贵的王冠，开始理解女儿的人生态度，而理解带来了和解，最后是她鼓励女儿打破传统，追求自我。电影好看归好看，我还是要指出，尽管皮克斯打着各种第一次的宣传口号，还是掩盖不了本片创意的缺乏，而这才是皮克斯动画最闪光的部分，会说话的玩具、会说话的汽车、收集孩子尖叫来发电的怪兽、热爱烹饪的小老鼠、收集地球废品的害羞机器人、会飞的房子，每一个都是让人浮想联翩的绝佳点子，可《勇敢传说》中追求自我的女孩、变成动物的父母、会魔法的老太太，这几个关键元素我们早就在宫崎骏的《千与千寻》中看过了，况且《勇敢传说》的故事并不比《千与千寻》更精彩。所以我总觉得《勇敢传说》好看虽好看，但无甚惊喜，没有看《》和《飞屋环游记》时忍不住赞叹的激动感觉。再次重申，我是个皮克斯脑残粉，真心不希望它变得太过迪士尼化，真心希望《赛车总动员2》是皮克斯的低谷，《勇敢传说》是调整回暖，下一部则是重回巅峰。

《金鱼》这本连环画是50开平装本，由连环画出版社出版，讲述了这样一个传说故事：从前有个布商，续娶了一个妻子（她带来一个小孩）。有一次孩子网到一条金鱼，他不忍带回，便把它放了。回到家他对布商一说，布商知道这条鱼很值钱，气得要把孩子杀死。孩子就逃跑了。孩子在路上遇到了一位青年并和他一同除掉妖魔抢出公主，在青年的帮助下，这个孩子和公主结了婚。后来才知道青年原来是金鱼变的。孩子把他母亲接来，一起过着安乐的日子。画家刘仲文，男，1944年生，祖籍天津武清。中国美术家协会会员，毛主席纪念堂美术专业研究员，中华艺龙国际书画研究院副院长，齐白石艺术大师再传弟子。自受庭训，酷爱文学和书画艺术。在美术思想理论上受著名美术教育家、雕塑大师刘开渠多年教诲，受益颇深。1977年在毛主席纪念堂从事美术创作、展览设计、画册编辑。1986年入齐白石艺术函授学院深造，后拜齐白右大师之子善名画家齐良迟为师并成为人室弟子。擅长齐派写意花鸟兼工书法。其国画作品笔力遒劲、蕴涵丰富，显现出文人画所具有的文学修养和书法功力。其作品多次在国内外重大展览中参展并获奖。1992年，国画《九衢风土带花香》被作为国礼赠送朝鲜国家领导人金正日；1999年国画《玉珠飘香》被中国驻挪威大使馆陈列，2001年荣获联合国美术大展铜奖。大型画册《中南海书画集》、《毛主席纪念堂珍藏书画集》《齐白石与当代名家书画集》等均有作品入编。出版有《收藏陈列中国名家书画的艺术殿堂》、《画坛巨匠齐白石的艺术道路和爱国情操》、《刘仲文书画集》等多部典籍。北京电视台《书坛画苑》栏目《海内与海外》、《艺术人生》杂志及《人民日报》、《人民政协报》、《经济日报》等报刊对其艺术成就有专访报道。京东服务不错，好评！

《瓦尔登湖》是那种彻底拒绝浮躁的好书，有一种返璞归真的美丽蕴藏在里面，你要心无杂念地去捧读，心如止水还止水的沉静去思去读才能懂得这样做的好处。书中隽语不断迭出，犹如涓涓细流注入当下人们的心灵的荒原，给人以一种清新冲淡通脱之美的感受，自然，除了自然，好像什么也没有了。自然是存在之家，而人以自然之家为家。《瓦尔登湖》是真正伟大的作品，它能够直通你的心灵，深入你的骨髓，熔铸到你的整个品性和人格，甚至成为你生命的一部分，当然，你得用心去进入。梭罗在《湖》中这样写到：瓦尔登湖的风景是卑微的，虽然很美，却并不是宏伟的，不常去玩的人，不住在它岸边的人未必能被它吸引住；但是这样一个湖以深邃和清澈著称，值得给予突出的描写。这是一个明亮深绿色的湖，半英里长，周围约一英里又四分之三，面积约61英亩半。通脱自然再平常不过了，但它时刻唤醒着我们记忆中的那份风景。他说话语气很轻，带着几分痴傻：我也没有像鸣禽一般地歌唱，我只静静地微笑，笑我幸福无涯。梭罗眼中的湖不仅仅是一个湖，而且是一个充满着性情的湖。因为一个湖是风景中最美的，最有表情的姿容。它是大地的眼睛；望着它的人可以侧出他自己天性的深浅。湖所产生的湖边的树木就睫毛一样的镶边，而四周森林蓊郁的群山和山岸是它的浓密突出的眉毛。多少次，我也这样欣赏风景，我的心中的湖，然而我却常常是失望的。后来我明白了，世界上只有一个瓦尔登湖，而且是梭罗的瓦尔登湖。其实，世界上的每一个人都在寻找自己的瓦尔登湖。当然，梭罗不是那种不食人间烟火的隐士，而我们却从他那里发现许多的光亮。他在《阅读篇》中写到：一个人如果不能相信每一天都有一个比亵渎过的更早，更神圣的曙光时晨，他一定是已经对于生命失望的了，正在摸索着一条降入黑暗的道路。在《春天》中他又说：我们需要看到我们突破自己的限度，需要在一些我们从未漂泊过的牧场上自由地生活。好像他在给我们众生指明道路，那末，走你自己的路吧。梭罗好像对生活有一种妙悟，是的，一种真正的人生妙悟。这种妙悟不是从天而降，而是从瓦尔登湖那里思得来的。诚如他在书中的《结论》指出那样：至少我是从实验中了解到：一个人若能自信地向他梦想的方向行进，努力经营他所期望的生活，他是可以获得通常还意想不到的成功的。如果有谁认为梭罗仅仅是个隐士，那他便忽视了他还是位抨击时弊的演说家和诲人不倦的教师；如果有谁妄想从《瓦尔登湖》里获得亲近泥土的捷径，那么就借问牧童和鹧鸪。在白昼的繁忙生活之中，我有时读它还读不进去，似乎我异常喜欢的在本书忽然又不那么可爱可喜了，似乎觉得它什么好处也没有，甚至变得将信将疑起来。可是黄昏以后，心情渐渐的寂寞和恬静下来，再读此书，则忽然又颇有味，而看的就是白天看不出来辨不出来味道的章节，语语惊人，字字闪光，沁人心肺，动我哀肠。到了夜深人静，万籁无声之时，这《瓦尔登湖》毫不晦涩，清澈见底，吟诵之下，不禁为之神往了。徐迟在《译序》中这样的道出了读此书的真谛。白天，黄昏，夜深人静，在这三种不同的时间读书，自然会产生不同的心境，得到的味道自然也是不同的了。我当然没有这样的读过这本书，但我能体会到个中的滋味。好像我要说的话都被他说尽了一样。而我又能说什么呢。唉唉，恨不能相见。梭罗《瓦尔登湖》的意蕴，恐怕只有在日本文学中才能找到同感的典型。尤其是川端的小说，怎一个细字，淡字了得，那是另一种审美体验的全面与细致。梭罗诗意的散文与川端散文的小说都要在虚静中阅读的，在虚静中才能体悟到其中的好处。梭罗是要主张回归自然的。但梭罗与陶渊明不同，梭罗到瓦尔登湖去，并非想去做永久返归自然的隐士，而仅是他崇尚人的完整性的表现之一。当代散文家赵丰在《想象梭罗》中精彩的道出了二人的区别，他这样的写道：他真的想做隐士吗？为何不到人烟罕至的更遥远的森林去？我的答案是梭罗是一个思想家，而非陶渊明般的隐士。陶渊明构建了桃花源，是想自得其乐，而梭罗呢？他却是通过独居来解析人类的心灵。区别就在于此，从这点来说，梭罗的境界远远高于陶渊明的境界。他的清静和陶渊明的清静有着本质的区别。是的，这两份悠然或恬静是不一样的。而梭罗更叫我着迷。回归自然，，回到自然中去，做一个自然中的人，一个自然的人，去感悟自然的妙处，领略自然的真谛，这是他一生的追求。他窥到了自然的堂奥，好像在笑，笑我们芸芸众生。梭罗致力于把日常生活的每时每刻变成艺术性的，一种审美的生活，它依靠的是自己：自己耕作，自己收获，感受四季的变化，为春天的到来而欢欣，他倾听，他真正体验着自己，把美学贯彻到他的生活，他的写作中，他说：片刻的美好经验比一座月亮一般高的纪念碑还要值得记忆。他是从审美体验中获得真理和伦理。

从南至北约1000公里，从东到西也约1000公里，顶着法兰西名字的这片近乎规整六边形的土地，与当今世界的大国相比，似乎很小。就面积而言，排名第37，人口位列第13。但在过去的数个世纪里，法国在文明和世界事件的进程中扮演了第一流的角色，今天依然如此。从法兰西民族植根的这块奇异士地本身来寻求这种优越性的部分原因，如果不是为了表明某种荒唐的宿命论，还是颇有几分道理的。这片领土地理位置极佳，位居西欧心脏地带，而西欧间隔两千年二度成为重要文明和世界扩张的摇篮。它地处世界各大陆的十字路口。作为陆地，？与邻近广袤的欧亚大陆紧密相连作为滨海地带，四海波涛拍打而至，路通天下。由于这样的双重身份，它向所有的经营事业和所有的冒险活动敞开了胸怀。这片领土同样由于它多彩的风、貌和充满希冀而让人怦然心动，在此既有北部围垦地柔和淡定的灰调，也有地中海海角波光鳞鳞的闪亮，既有麦穗沉沉的大平原，也有欧洲最宏大的冰川。在所有这些累积的天赋之中，也许最终就是由于自然环境的无穷变幻和居住人群的多种多样才为人类提供了最诱人的前景，才保证了我们的国土不仅具有吸引人的魅力，而且为我们国家提供了在历史上多次被开？的多重可能性。法国属于温带的国度，但气候却千差万别，同时包含有海洋型、大陆型和地中海型气候的影响。它位于欧洲的顶端，其地质地貌似乎是整个欧洲大陆的汇总其中有广袤连绵的北方平原，有亘古不变的古老高原，还有俯瞰深谷的年轻山脉。这些因素以特有的方式结合在一起，以致于它们的效应进一步强化，从而赋予我们领土的各个部分以更鲜明的个性有些低矮丘陵勉强隆起的宽广平原占据了整个西部，它们为海洋势力的渗透提供了场地而与此对应的是，地中海气候特征却由于庇护着东南平原的高山屏障而进一步得到增强。如果笼而统之地描述整个法国，有可能使这种非常丰富的自然多样性消失殆尽。相反，如果我们依着景致的变化，逐个地区地来刻画，就可能不会发生这样的危险。

京东买书价格优，送货快，优惠活动也多，正版有保证，多读书增长知识。高尔基曾说：书是人类进步的阶梯。的确，看一本好书就像在和一个高尚的人谈话，书在每个地方，每个时代都有着重要的地位，包含着无穷无尽的知识。一个家庭没有书，就等于一间房子没有窗子。可想而知书在日常生活中的重要性。它像一束阳光，一扇风景。不仅可以提高我们的生活情趣，而且，使生活变的更加丰富多彩，有声有色。我们通过读书丰富知识，增长见识，让生活过得更充实，更有意义。在书中我们可以学习许多小窍门，解决生活中遇到的小难点。几百上千年前的古人已经知道了读书的好处，有许多热爱读书的故事都流传至今，其中王羲之的故事非常值得我们深思相传。一天中午，王羲之正在读书，书童送来馍馍和蒜泥，他因为看书入了迷，竟拿着一块馍沾了墨汁就往嘴里送，错把墨汁当蒜泥吃了，还说：今天的蒜泥真香啊！通过这个故事，我深深体会到了读书的重要性，前人能做到读书废寝忘食的地步，为后人留下了许多宝贵的知识，财富，我们有什么不好好读书而沉迷于游戏，电视？与他们相比我们不感到惭愧吗？读书的过程是艰难的，也是快乐的。渐渐的，在读书中我有了熟读唐诗三百首，不会吟诗也会吟的才气，感受到了风萧萧兮易水寒，壮士一去兮不复还的豪气，体会到了天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来的傲气在读书的过程中，我的作文水平也得到了提高，以前，我写作文时，总是不知道该用哪些词。所以老去问妈妈，妈妈就说：孩子，你应该多看些书，哪一个作家像冰心，老舍都不是破了万卷书，才下笔如有神的呢？从此，我就天天看书，记录书中的好词，好句，体会作者的思想感情。果然，一段时间过后，我的作文水平就有一点点提高。书是人类一生的朋友，在哪里都有极其崇高的地位，正如三字经中所言人之初，性本善。性相近，习相远。苟不教，性乃迁。教之道，贵以专。充分说明了读书的人后天的影响。读书有这么多的好处，我们有什么理由不好好读书么？

These headphones have been of outstanding value and I am quite tempted to give them 5 stars. I haven't had this much fun listening to headphones in a long time. The first thing I noticed is a better than average precision balancing of sound between the two drivers, and separation that stands out from other headphones in this range. At first the headphones are a little on the harsh side, but after some listening for a week they have seemed to become more dynamic. For being non-amplified, these headphones have managed to provide quite punchy and lively bass without the rest of the sound being muddled or losing accuracy. Frequency sweeps across the spectrum have been very impressive. Noises, horn stabs, shouting sounds, claps, and bright sounding music sound great on these. I have been able to hear different layers of sound while still enjoying that aggressive bass. Another thing that blew me away was the musicality of these headphones. I'm not an audiophile, or one of these people that claims to have golden ears... but I think that musicality really goes a long way. There was noticeable warmth in the mids and lows that made me want to keep listening to music, even other styles I've never heard before. And then I look back at the price and I am astounded. These headphones easily sound better than many others that are over $100. And comfort is the best of any Skullcandy's I've encountered so far. These headphones seem to be an improvement in every way over my Hesh 2s and SkullCrushers. The elements in them seem of considerably better quality and are noticeably more balanced. Sound isolation is pretty good once you get these things completely on your ears, definitely not the best. But certainly no complaints. The only downside is that the sound is by no means flat. These are not studio reference headphones. Parts of low frequencies and highs will definitely be boosted and can lead to a bit of listening fatigue after long listening sessions.

So close, and yet so far. The dock is solid, and having the "case" to hold the tablet so that it will charge in the dock is well thought out. The problem? The charge contacts on the back of the case are very small. If the tablet isn't exactly aligned with those charge contacts, not only will it not charge, but it won't work in Echo Show mode either (since it needs to be charging for that to function). Aligning it with those contacts isn't that difficult, but it does require looking at the back of the tablet while you dock it, which is a pain. If Amazon had just put a small bump in the middle of the dock at the bottom, and a corresponding notch on the side of the case, it would line up easily every time. Bottom line, if you don't plan to take the tablet off the dock much, then this will work fine. If you're planning on removing and returning it with some frequency, the difficulty in docking it properly will annoy the heck out of you. One other note: the microphones in the tablet are clearly inferior to those in the Echo/Echo Show/Echo Dot, which isn't hugely surprising, actually. I have to speak much louder and more clearly for Alexa commands to be understood than with my Echo Dot.

I hate to leave negative reviews, but this product is being falsely advertised as being a direct replacement battery for the Sena 10S and 20S! See included collage photos with measurements included. The battery with the letters "XK" on it is the OEM battery that is being replaced. The battery with the letters "LP" on it, is the battery from this seller. The last collage shows the measurements of where the battery needs to be placed. The 1st and second photos show the width and length measurements. The replacement battery from this seller is not only 1.09mm wider than the original OEM battery, it is also a WHOPPING 3.07mm longer! While these amounts don't seem like much, they mean the world when it comes to small handheld electronics. The last thing you need is for a battery "bouncing" around inside a handheld electronic device! The last image shows the maximum length and width measurements for the battery to sit flush on the circuit board where it needs to be attached via double sided tape. The replacement battery is 1.68mm longer and .7mm wider than the maximums allowed for the battery to sit flush with the circuit board. I'm returning this battery along with the one I got for a 10C as it too is exceeds the maximum dimensions to fit properly. DISAPPOINTED!!!

I use the BDP-S790 with an XBR6 TV connected via HDMI through a Sony STR-DA5300ES AV Receiver. So, I cannot comment on 3D performance. This is a great piece of hardware that loads Blu-ray disks very fast and plays them well. It also does a very good job streaming video from my home network and reads and scrolls through folder and file lists quickly. It plays a good variety of media file types. Despite this hardware performance this product is missing a few media player features that it really should have such as the ability to read playlists and to define a queue of files (a temporary playlist) for later playing. In other words this product does not organize the media, it just plays them. I'm guessing this is a reflection of Sony design goals. I ran into a few glitches that may be corrected by future firmware updates. Some of my Blu-ray disks (Band of Brothers box set) would not play and would cause the product to power off or go into an infinite loop. The work-around was to set the Gracenote media identification to "manual". Also, my .mp4 files created by my Sanyo Xacti HD camcorder would play from my Western Digital My Book World Edition NAS, but not from my Western Digital My Book Live NAS. The former uses a Twonky media server, while the latter's media server was not branded but could be Western Digital software. I'm not sure what the cause for this is, but my [[ASIN:B005KOZNBW Western Digital WD TV Live Streaming Media Player - WDBHG70000NBK-HESN]] plays these files successfully from both NAS sources. The BDP-S790 successfully streams .mp4 and .m2ts AVCHD files created by Nero Vision from both NAS sources. Photos are displayed at full resolution on my HDTV. This is now my preferred device for viewing my photo collection. I am very pleased with the variety and ease of use of internet services. In conclusion, this product is an excellent piece of hardware and does a great job playing Blu-ray disks and delivering internet content. It is very good a streaming media from the home network. It lacks media organizer features that are common to many media players. Overall I'm very happy with my purchase.

First and foremost, please subscribe to my YouTube channel at transformational gaming. You can also hit me up on Twitter @transform_gamer if you want to discuss any of my reviews. There's good and bad about SR5014. Let's start with the bad. The app is not all that impressive. Difficult to connect to the Marantz AV receiver, the application is somewhat plain looking and is a little clunky. But that's about it when it comes to negativity about this receiver. Outside of that, this av receiver is probably the best 7.2 channel receiver out right now given the price of 999. You can say other things like not having an a way to spread vocals to the front as opposed to the center channel in surround mode. It sounds really stupid but I hear that Denon has the same problem. And Gene from audioholics has been protesting this problem, so I hope at some point they make a compromise. But, with a 4 volt output on the preouts, the SR5014 has some serious pop. My previous AV receiver was a the Onkyo RC260. So, I just wanted a receiver with preouts. When I bought this, I was amazed by the difference in quality. The preouts that went to the my powered subwoofer have noticeable clarity. The surrounds have definition and each channel just have a real punch. Maybe I had a poor receiver to begin with, with the RC260, but now I feel like I can enjoy my front stage without immediately going out and purchasing an external amplifier. I have not experienced equipment failure like the others have reviewed with this receiver. But, I must say that for those who are not Atmos guys, (this receiver can do Atmos btw) this receiver provides a great 5.2 surround solution in bi-amp mode. There are so many configurations. You will have the pleasure setting up your receiver for the coveted sweet spot. Also, another quality that was so refreshing was the EQ setting for each channel. I've been looking for an av receiver that has an EQ for years since the middle 90s. And, I can play with and EQ each channel? Man - I am just so flattered with this receiver. Great product. I may step up to 11.x in the future, but I'm just not interested in having that many channels to manage. Seem like that would be a nightmare. And how much content has 5 channels mixed in its content, let alone 11. Okay up mix is a thing... but how much accuracy is in that processing? Okay, this is a review, so I'll get back on track. If you are good with 7 channels, get this receiver. Marantz is the best. I'll be definitely looking to purchase my next av receiver from Marantz.

Review for Sony UBP-X700 (4K BD player) Video quality is excellent, as expected. Setup is easy. It streams quite well. Some cons, though: contrary to what is said in the specs, both in the online specs and in the user's manual, it will NOT play either TrueHD audio or E-AC3 if they are in mkv files. For all I know, they may or may not play them on commercial disks, but I would assume they tested those audio codecs on commercial disks. I was in a 2 hour chat with Sony's tech support trying to figure out why it won't play TrueHD (which is the only Dolby audio that is lossless), and they finally gave up, with the final word being "It's supposed to play TrueHD, but we don't guarantee it." Make what you will of that. I was about to just put up with it, and then I streamed an episode of The Flintstones with E-AC3 audio (extended Dolby, still lossy but with more digital info than plain Dolby), and it won't play that either, whether on disk or while streaming. That was a deal-breaker, as that is a very common audio codec. It will play DTS.HDMA audio tracks, and this player makes that sound great. That's close to lossless, but most UHD movies are going to use TrueHD going forward. Another issue, which may be common in other BD players, is that the USB port is 2.0. That would be OK, too, since 2.0 can easily feed fast enough to keep up with even UHD, except that it won't read a 3.0 thumb drive at all! Lack of compatibility may or may not be an issue for you. USB is supposed to be backward compatible, but not with this player. I sent it back, because if it won't play lossless audio in an mkv file, it just won't do. My older Samsung BD player has issues reading home-burned BluRay Dual Layer disks, but at least it will handle all major audio codecs on single layer disks. So bottom line: if you all you intend to do is play commercial disks, and stream standard definition video or music, this guy will serve you well. Beyond that, perhaps not so much.

I ordered one of these for my daughter's phone and one for my phone, and we received them on October 5. It's currently November 28. When I mentioned this at home, my daughter said that apps she'd put on her memory card kept being seen as uninstalled on her phone. I've been religiously backing up new photos since then, which is good, since tonight most of my galleries briefly showed up as corrupted, and then the phone ceased to recognize that there was a card inserted, at all. Upon checking the card on my computer, I discovered that it's now being seen as unformatted. Everything's totally gone. This is the second memory card I've had in my phone, and I had zero issues with the old one; I only switched because I needed more space. My daughter's card is still functioning in the sense that her phone sees that it's inserted, but most of what she tries to store on it disappears. In summary, I find it shockingly bold that this is referred to as a "Memory Card", since mine doesn't even remember being formatted eight weeks ago, and neither of them remember what we've saved on them. When I went to the return/refund page on Amazon, it informed me that the window for returning these closed on November 4. However, upon calling customer service, I was issued a full refund immediately, so thank you to Amazon for that. It doesn't replace the photos of my son's field trip to the science center or of my kids trick-or-treating on Halloween, but at least now I can purchase memory cards which will hopefully operate as advertised.

My wife and I do street interviews for our web sites, and I needed something to lower the volume of my wireless mics. I was reluctant to purchase the Azden Cam-3, because of some of the very negative reviews it received. However, I took a chance anyway. Here is my response to the negative feedback givers: It's definitely possible that you received one that was DOA. However, those who gave this product negative feedback for other reasons do not understand what the Azden Cam-3 does, and does not do. 1. It does NOT increase the volume of a microphone. How can it? It is passive--no battery and no electrical connection. 2. It does NOT hum, or add any other noise or interference. Let me restate this--it's passive, so it cannot add hum or any other extraneous noise. 3. What it's meant to do, it does perfectly! It adjusts the volume of a microphone that might be louder than others that are connected, to create a uniform volume. It does NOT increase the volume of the others, just lowers the volume of the overly loud one(s). 4. It's a perfect size--a little larger than a Digital Video Cassette. I easily attached it to the side strap on my Panasonic DVC30. I do wish that ALL the inputs were stereo, but it's not that big a deal. As it is, inputs 1 and 2 are mono, and input 3 and the output are stereo. Bottom line: It does exactly what the AD says it does!!! My only regret is that I did not buy it sooner.

I recently built a new PC and went with a white theme for the first time. It looks great, but at the time it was hard to get a video card. I lucked out and was able to get a 3080 FE from Bestbuy to tide me over while I tried to get my hands on a white card that would better match my build. I love how the white Strix cards look, so once I was able to get one I bit the bullet and shelled out nearly $400 more than my FE cost to get this white Strix. The specs and reviews all make Strix out to be the best of the best, higher power limits, better build quality, superior cooling... So anyway... I got the card and was thrilled to hook it up. It's beautiful in my PC and much quieter than my FE model. I was very happy with my purchase at first.... It took a couple months before I got a good feel for the card and felt I was ready to review it. In this time, I have grown fairly disappointed in the card. Memory temps started off in the mid 80's when mining or benchmarking/heavy gaming. Now the memory is hitting 100c with the fan set at 80% luckily the fans are much quieter that the FE which would be screaming once over 75% fan. The card has also been growing less stable. It tends to crash at times of heavy use occasionally even causing my PC to fully restart. These are both problems I didn't encounter in the 4 months I used my Founders 3080, I mean sure, the FE memory did run warm, I had the repad it, and after repadding it max's at 84c mem temp but it's also a much cheaper card that's got a fraction of the cooler this Strix has. As for stability, the FE was perfectly stable, even with moderate overclocking and heavy use. There was a time I had it mining ether while I was playing Fallout 4 and it was getting 87mh/s while running the game in 1440p with no issue. All said and done, I may have just lost the silicon lottery or just been real unlucky, but either way, I am not satisfied with a card that had a $1080 MSRP before tax. It should perform better than the Founders Edition card and the fact it doesn't is extremely disappointing. So, it looks very nice in a white build and the fans are reasonably quiet.

I was in the market for a new laptop and fell in love with the cost and the specifications of this system – two that stood out were the dedicated video card with 4GB dedicated ram and the 1920 x 1080 full HD matte screen (the matte screen was very important to me). I was also happy to see that I could upgrade the RAM to 16GB, replace the hard drive with a solid state drive and use a hard drive caddy to put the 1 TB hard drive in as a secondary drive. Needless to say I immediately ordered the system, extra RAM and a caddy. I was really excited when my husband called me at work to say that the system had arrived. I was a bit disappointed that the RAM and caddy had been delayed and would not arrive until after the weekend. This turned out to be a godsend. Unlike a lot of other reviews I liked the plastic case and the texture of the case. The system started up perfectly, was a snap to set it up. Then the problems started. The NVidia graphics and the Intel graphics did not play well together. I could not open the NVidia control panel, the system would crash. I spent numerous hours searching for fixes with both NVidia and Acer support. Nothing worked. The only thing that would keep the system from crashing was to disable the NVidia card in the device manager. Side note -- the only games I play are World of Warcraft and SWGemu; both loaded up and played flawlessly when the NVidia card was disabled – so disappointed I never saw how they would run using the NVidia display. Anyway, disabling the adapter kind of defeats the purpose of having a dedicated card with 4GB of RAM. After working countless hours over the weekend with this system and using every trick that I know, the system would NOT run as intended and I returned it. Through my research I read that Windows 10 and NVidia Optimus are having problems. I have to have Windows 10 for my job, so installing Windows 8.1 would have not been a possible solution. I tried everything and nothing worked. The system would crash when the NVidia adapter was in use and this was totally unacceptable. I was not willing to wait to see if a Windows update or NVidia update would fix the problem or even to return the system for a replacement. If this sounds harsh, this is why: Several years ago I purchased an Acer laptop with a dedicated NVidia adapter and it also had problems. I stayed with that system waiting on promises that updates would solve the issue (which they did not) and finally NVidia said yes there were issues and they were fixing the issues with the desktop cards/adapters, but that laptop adapters changed to rapidly so they were doing nothing to resolve the issues my system was having with the adapter it came with. Acer’s only help was to tell me I should not have changed out the adapter – which was laughable as it could not be changed and came stock with the system. Anyway, due to the fact that these issues in the past were never resolved I did not care to chance a repeat of that fiasco and returned the system. If you were one of the lucky ones who had no problems with this system I believe that it has absolutely incredible specs and if it runs as expected it should be a killer system. On my system running only with the Intel graphics adapter I loved the matte screen (I hate glossy screens). And Acer customer service if you are reading this, it was my treatment from Acer in the previous situation listed above, that prompted me to return the laptop. I have not written Acer off, as I have an Acer Aspire Switch 10 with 64GB internal storage and 2GB RAM. I upgraded this little gem to Windows 10, and I use a 128 GB Micro SD card on which I save all my work and I have WOW installed, and that little system plays it pretty darn well (no raiding of course!) running it off of an SD card with 2GB RAM. I just had such high hopes for this system – but alas it was not meant to be.

Updated review 8/10/16 -- The modem still works fine, but just a word of warning regarding Comcast. I had issues with my phone service recently (no dial tone). After a LONG and ridiculous hassle with Comcast customer service reps both online and on the phone (who continued to tell me that I had never installed this modem and that the CMAC number did not exist in their system, which was absolutely not true -- just read my review below and you will see that I registered this modem with Comcast), I finally had to go in person to the local Comcast office. They were able to find the modem in the system and re-activate it. The CMAC number had been typed into the wrong field apparently. So the problem was not with the modem but with Comcast, whom I think does not like it when customers buy their own modem.... Original review: I have wanted to buy a telephony modem for a few years now, but was afraid because of all of the negative comments from people who have had nightmare experiences with Comcast. It was enough to make me decide to keep renting a modem from Comcast. However, in the past few weeks, I have gotten a letter and multiple phone calls from Comcast, telling me that my old modem was not allowing me to get the internet speed I am paying for. Plus, I noticed that my internet speed seemed to be getting slower (the comcast internet speed test showed that my download speed was only 19.59, and I should be at 50). So I decided to make the move and buy a modem. I literally looked at all 486 reviews on this modem before purchasing. I saved $55 and got a used one (in "Very Good" condition), which made me a bit nervous because I had read a review that said that if the modem was already in the Comcast system, it might not work for me. My modem arrived today (in 2 days) thanks to Amazon Prime and I was excited to try it. It looked brand new -- would never guess that it was used. It's Sunday, so I called the Comcast activation number -- 855-OK-BEGIN (855-652-3446) -- just to make sure they were working on a Sunday before I got started. The agent was very helpful when I told her why I was calling (good sign!) -- she said activating my purchased modem would be easy - just to call back once everything was plugged in. I followed the instructions that "Gordon" wrote in his Amazon review (thank you Gordon), but everything did not go the way it went for him: So -- this is how it went: 1) Installed the battery in my TM822G 2) Unplugged the old RCA Thomson modem and removed the coax, phone, and ethernet connections 3) Removed the ethernet cable from my wireless router 4) Connected everything to the 822G -- phone cable goes in the Tel 1/2 jack -- and connected the ethernet directly to my laptop (which was not turned on yet) 5) Plugged the new modem into the electrical outlet and waited for the lights to come on. Turned on my laptop. The Comcast agent had told me during my earlier call to wait until the 1st and 3rd lights come on. It took about 10 minutes. 6) It took a couple of trys to get my internet browser to work, but when it did, I went to the [...] site and logged in. 7) This is where things did not go as planned. I was not able to log in -- I got a message: "This account is not eligible for automated activation. Please call us at 1-855-OK-BEGIN" 8) Using my cell phone, I called the number and instead of going through the menu of commands, I said: "Speak to a representative." I was connected to a live agent named Princess fairly quickly. I told her that I wanted to activate a purchased modem, and she asked for the CMAC number, which was conveniently taped to the top of my modem. 9) After verifying my account information, she sent a signal to the modem. We waited for the lights to stop blinking -- just took a minute or 2. She asked me to check the internet -- it was working! 10) She then said she would set up my telephone service (unlike other Amazon reviewers, I did not need to call a different number -- the same agent took care of everything). She sent a signal for the phone line, and after about a minute, the light came on. She asked me to go to my landline, check for a dial tone, and place a call. It worked! 11) She then said that she would put me on hold and call me on my landline. She did, and when we connected, she asked me to disconnect our cell phone call to save my battery and minutes (I thought this was a nice touch!) 12) I asked her if the $8 modem rental charge would be removed from my bill. She said that I needed to return the old modem in order to remove the charge. So even though Comcast tells you that you don't need to return the old modem, she advised that I should return it to a Comcast office (or mail it back) in order to get the rental charge removed. 13) DONE! I thanked her and she gave me a troubleshooting number to call in case I have any problems: 800-934-6489, option 1 for Tech Support. I don't think I will need this number! I switched the ethernet from my laptop back to the wireless router. Everything still perfect. IT WAS EASY AND PAINLESS. If it was painful before, I think that Comcast has gotten their act together. The agent (Princess) was very nice and helpful. The call only took 15 minutes. I immediately went online to check my internet speed. It is now up to 44.56 from 19.59! I am so thrilled. My only regret is that I should have done this sooner.

The more audio products I am exposed to, the more I appreciate the Audioengine D1. I've tried other DACs on Amazon that cost a fraction of what the Audioengine cost, but I had problems with all of them, such as buzzing and hissing sounds. Moreover, even my Bose Companion 5 speakers (which I paid $400 for and has a built-in DAC and a headphone jack) has distracting white noise even when no audio is present). The Audioengine thus fills a vital role in my setup as far as powering my headphones and giving me good clean audio. There is ZERO hissing or white noise even at high volume. The build quality is very nice and you can feel the difference immediately if you've ever held cheaper no-name DACs. I have two complaints, both relatively minor, but to me, a bigger deal considering the price tag. (1) the included USB cord is WAY TOO SHORT - it's like two feet long or something. How can ANYBODY use this cord if they hope to put the device on a desktop and connect it to a computer that is on the ground? The cord is useless and the decision to include such a short cord just boggles my mind and makes me question Audioengine's commitment to its customers. I had to go out and get a longer cord just so I could use a device I paid almost $200 for. And it isn't the type of USB cable you probably have tons of. It's the type of cable that you typically hook up a print with, so you cant just grab your cable that you use for your cell phone or something. Seriously - who uses a two-foot long chord? They only reason you'd do that is if you plan put the device on top of your PC. But then, how would you even access the volume knob? Dumb. (2) there is NO ac adapter included (unless you want to pay Audioengine 18 dollars to send you one). This means you HAVE to plug this device into your computer via USB, even if you aren't using USB as the audio source. For example, I use my motherboard's optical line out and feed that directly to the Audioengine D1. I assumed I could power the device separately via my wall outlet (which even the cheaper DACs I tried before could do). Nope - I still have plug the USB cable into my computer in order to power the device. I don't like having extra USB devices plugged into my computer that aren't unnecessary, so I went out and purchased an AC adapter for the USB connection to free up the USB slot on my computer. For a device that costs almost $200, both of my complaints (though minor in the grand scheme of things) are pretty inexcusable in my opinion, thus the 4-star rating rather than 5. The short USB cord really gets to me. The AC adapter I can understand because the option to use your PC's USB slot to power the device is there. Most importantly though, on the quality of the device itself, I have no complaints, and I would recommend this product. But you'll have to, at the very least, go out and buy a longer USB chord.

These headphones allow me to click up or down to get the exact volume I want. Since I frequently turn down the volume during commercials or extra-loud scenes this is particularly useful. The controls are also large, raised, and very easy to locate while you are wearing the headphones - no more fumbling to find tiny flat buttons! The headphones are a bit tight at times (I wear glasses) but not uncomfortably so and are easily adjustable. I also miss the automatic on/off that used to be common on older headphones but seem to be missing in the more recent ones. This is the only HDMI 2.0 KVM I've been able to find. If you need HDMI 2.0 support, this is the one you want. Note that it does not support DVI monitors, although DVI computers are okay. Also, be aware that some 4K monitors can only do 4K over DisplayPort because their HDMI is limited to 1.0 speeds. If you have a monitor like that, this KVM will not work for you. This KVM works perfectly with my 3440x1440@60Hz LG monitor. It has had no issues with any resolution the connected computers have thrown at it. Audio works well, too. I have not tested the remote, since it didn't come with batteries, and I don't have the right coin-cells laying around. It would be nice if the remote took AA or AAA batteries instead. I have also not used the included HDMI/USB cables, since they look like garbage to me. I did examine the included cables with a multimeter and noticed that the USB cables did not connect the frame ground. I do not recommend using cables like that because it is possible hot-plugging them could damage your equipment. Like many KVMs, the emulated keyboard and mouse allow zero-latency switching and allow hot-keys and mouse gestures for switching inputs. However, also like other KVMs, the emulated keyboard and mouse only support basic keyboards and mice. Anything beyond the vanilla 104-key keyboard is ignored. Anything beyond a simple mouse is ignored (3 buttons + scroll up/down). Unfortunately, if you are using the emulated keyboard, then the first key-press after a long idle period is dropped! The switched USB port does not have this issue. This annoyed me enough that I moved both my keyboard and mouse to the switched USB port (using the USB hub in my monitor, of course, since there is only one switched USB port on the KVM). Switching using the front panel is a bit annoying since you can only cycle through the four ports with each press, so I bought a four-key X-Keys KVM keyboard. It's tiny, and can be programmed to send the right key sequence to the KVM to switch directly to each input.

This is one of several digital cameras I have used over the years. I did a lot of homework and a lot of reviewing before selecting this camera. It arrived just in time for an international trip that I had planned. (FYI..the pictures from this trip came out great!) I am not a photographer--I am just a regular girl who loves to snap pictures of her friends and her surroundings. For this purpose, this camera is wonderful. The picture quality is superb in the daylight, the controls are easy to use, and the camera is very small and light-weight. I enjoy using the Zoom feature and it does a decent job. The optical zoom is very good. I will say the digital zoom is fair at best. The pictures become a bit grainy with the digital zoom. This is one reason I did not give this camera 5 stars. Another reason this camera does not get five stars is because of the responsiveness of the zoom. When using the optical zoom, the control is almost too sensitive and it zooms and unzooms very quickly, often more than you want. When you cross the "bridge" to the digital zoom, the zoom control is VERY slow. Another thing making this a four star camera, is that the quality of pictures at night is poor. Obviously, when what you are photographing is close and you have the flash, things are fine. Overall, I'd rate this camera very good. The entire kit that I bought I'd actually rate as excellent. It comes with several useful accessories (for me the most useful have been the USB flash card adapter and carrying case) and for a good price. The price for the entire kit here is almost equal to the price of the camera alone in most stores I visited. I can see why this probably isn't the camera for a very serious photographer, but I am very pleased with my purchase.

I have used this radio and light for a number of years now. I have used the USB charging, solar and hand crank functions for recharging as well as the radio, light and power bank. The unit recharges through USB fairly quickly. There is a flashlight with multiple brightness settings and an SOS function. The radio reception can be decent for what is deemed a "weather radio". I like the fact that this radio rotates between the time and frequency as most radios do not display the time once the radio is operating. I like the fact you can turn on the WX mode at will. Unfortunately, this unit is really misleading in terms of charging via solar and hand crank. These features are only a big gimmick. It is not possible to get from one bar to two bars with any amount of solar charging. I have placed this radio on the window with full sun for eight hours and the bars never increased. I have also attempted to recharge the unit by hand cranking. Again, I am not able to see much difference without tiring my hands. The battery did finally die and the bad part is that despite it being an 18650 battery, it has proprietary connections with wires soldered to it. There is no way of replacing this battery without going back to the manufacturer for a replacement. Unfortunately, I have checked their website and they no longer sell this battery. They have somehow upgraded their unit so it can now accept any 18650 battery. While this is beneficial for new users, someone with an older unit will be forced to throw away a decent radio in order to reap the benefits of a replaceable battery. Midland Radio, if you are listening, I would hopefully get a replacement radio with the upgrade to the non-proprietary connectors in exchange for this review.

Guide: Its good to have a capacitor such as this on any high power car audio system. It will help smooth out the current draw from your battery, increasing the life of the battery and the life of your alternator. If your lights are dimming you NEED one of these! A good rule of thumb for sizing a capacitor is 500 watt RMS total amplification per 1 Farad minimum. So if you have one 500 watt RMS amplifier you need 1 Farad. If you have two 300 watt amplifiers you have a total of 600 watts and need 1.2 Farad. That being said bigger is better! Installing 2 Farad for a 300 watt amp will still work great. Low-quality discs. Most attempts to write data waste a disc or two before being successful; I'm estimating that, out of my hundred discs, I'll wind up successfully writing to about forty. Using a different computer, a different burner, a different operating system makes no apparent difference in success rates. If you're comparing rates for blank DVDs, you shouldn't be comparing this to other hundred-packs; you should be comparing them to fifty-pack spools while keeping your fingers crossed and remembering that you're also signing up for the labor of throwing away half or more of the discs in the spool. Remember when one of the perks of buying a spool of blank DVDs was that you then had an empty spool in which you could store the DVDs you had that were no longer blank? Not here: It's not apparent from the product photo, but this is just a flimsy plastic bottom, a flimsy plastic top, a flimsy spindle connecting them, and piece of paper wrapped around the discs. Not only have they saved a few pennies cutting out the perk of providing a storage solution for the DVDs they sold you once they've had data burned to them -- and, incidentally, requiring you to fork out for some way of storage for the DVDs you burned, which will certainly cost you more than it would have cost Philips to provide a decent storage case for the DVDs they're selling you. In fact, the spindle construction is so flimsy that the flimsy plastic spine connecting the two flimsy plastic plates snapped halfway through the spool, so now I've got a half-stack of blank DVDs sitting on my desk without even the minimal protection from dust and scratches that the crappy spool was previously providing. Shame on Philips for lending their name to this crap.

The LAX20 will prioritize the WAN signal, and if no WAN connection, it'll failover to the cell networks. Perfect solution. The failover process takes approx 60 seconds, so there is unfortunately downtime when switching. Still automatic, though! Another note: I originally bought the LAX20 for compatibility with Google Fi (uses all three Sprint, T-Mobile, and AT&T). I have since ditched Google Fi for the cheaper and better alternative US Mobile. I took a gamble and went with US Mobile's Verizon plan, which offers "Unlimited All" without data throttling. The LAX20 works with the Verizon network! I read reviews on here that said contrary, but I have first-hand experience that it does indeed work on Verizon. Just be sure to update your the LAX20 APN field to VZWINTERNET. All in all, it's a fast router and serves my needs very well.

I do not understand why the description says 1080p. Even the Image of the Product has 1080p highlighted. It will only project 1280*768. This is NOT 1080p and it is NOT 16:9. It is 16:10 at best which may seem like a small difference but at 100+ inches diagonal you will get a lot of wasted horizontal space. I must have played around with this thing for hours trying to figure out what was wrong, did I have a setting messed up, maybe my input device was not set correctly. Then I finally started looking closer at the description and it clearly says 1280*768. Aside from this and the fact that I will now have wasted space on my 100" 16:9 screen, the projector is very solid. The picture is clear and the sound is actually pretty good. I had some speakers set up ready to go and when I turned the projector on and played something the sound was so good I haven't bothered hooking them up. I probably still will but the point is you would be OKAY without any. My purpose was for playing video games in my office and not having to take over the living room TV to do so. So I am not watching big time movies or using it as a regular TV watching device. I pull down the screen, turn on the projector, play some PS4, turn it off, roll up the screen and back to the real world. My 3 stars is based on the inaccurate and confusing description. It doesn't help either that many of the Customer Answered questions confirm it is 16:9!! A simple measuring tape and calculator will prove that wrong. 16 divided by 9 is 1.78. Measure the projected picture and do the math, width divided by height. You get 1.67 which is 1280*768. Would love to be proven wrong and shown how to get true 16:9. I will happily update this review!!

Remember you get what you pay for in the realms of video quality. I ordered the 1080P POE (2Megapixel) system, therefore, I am very pleased. This system comes without a hard drive for saving data. The recorder can work with 2 drives if you have them. Get a good WD Purple drive or two for saving as they are designed for surveillance systems. I used an older 350 GB drive and can go over two weeks at a time recording all of the alerts I have had. larger capacity drives are great for longer stretches between overwrite. My technical level is higher than others and I have no qualms with drilling through brick and mortar to run cables. That said, I could work out the user interface on the NVR with little difficulty even without the manual. I did read the manual and as others have noted it appears to have used an early version of Google Translate for the English component. My friends in my works Technical Publishing department also had some fun reading through the manual. Every once in a while, they play a game of "Guess the Consumer Device" based on multiple manuals provided by the group. The manual states that you should verify each internal components connection. That is, make sure your cooling device inside the device is plugged in correctly. Mine was barely hanging on and needed to be seated properly. This could cause someone less confident with electronics to burn up a recorder and increase warranty claims. There were several connections like this which needed attention. Bare this in mind if you are using cost as your determining factor. If you are fine with these checks then this is a great device! Probably my biggest complaint was with the cables. They cables were rolled in nicely sized sets. However, the cable was then collapsed to save size and wrapped (not rolled) so tight that the inner cables were nearly crimped over/crushed. This could cause some data quality and connections issues if you are not careful when unrolling the cables. TAKE THE TIME to NOT crimp/fold over the cables when stretching them out. An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. While I can create my own cables from scratch, most cannot and why create one more point of failure when you can avoid it? Each cable was clearly labeled in length (15 or 25 meter cables). Plan your system setup to account for these cable lengths if you cannot or will not create your own cables from scratch. That is, put your recorder where it will reach each camera location. Setup of the system was a breeze (IMHO). One cable per camera (the power over Ethernet) and the cable ends have some acceptable weatherproofing connectors. I ran the network throughout my house and left plenty of growth ability in my hardware location. My cables run per most standard premise wiring conventions, so unsightly cables are kept to a minimum. Again, plan your recorder and camera locations carefully if you wish to avoid unsightly cables. Electronic setup was also a breeze (IMHO). It is very plug-and-play to plug-and-chug. you will want to have a local monitor available near the recorder when adjusting the settings for the cameras. Take the time to review your cameras areas which are watched for motion. You will get many unwanted alerts if you don't cut out high traffic areas of little importance. Things like freshly made spider webs on a breezy day could keep your system recording non stop. I believe the user interface is rather intuitive for MOST things. There could be some re-grouping of features, but that is more my preference. Camera installation was actually very easy - 3 screws per camera. Each camera came with the proper size allen wrench for snugging the camera into the desired look angle. Not much to be said here. I ran all of my cameras in a single uninterrupted day by myself. That included drilling a few holes in some bricks and eaves/overhangs for cable runs. The cameras blend real well with my home, and are unobtrusive. They are visible deterrents, but not gaudy when installed properly. Picture quality: Yet again, you get what you pay for. I don't recommend anything below the 1080P system. Something like 900 or 700 tv lines (tvl) will never give you desired quality images. This is not the movies or television. Real life cameras don't do what you see on CSI or NCIS. 1080P is a minimum. 2 megapixel up to 5 megapixel will give you awesome images also and great zoom capabilities. I also say stick with POE (Power Over Ethernet) for cables as they are easy to connect and sturdy single cable connections. BNC (the cctv standard) is good, but you will not get the quality images you get from Ethernet. XMEye app. Actually a nice little app. I have it on apple and android tablets as well as on android phones. The images are standard quality when going over the air (cellular), but are HD when on a wifi. The motion is as smooth as you should expect from cellular, somewhat jumpy, but the pictures, day or night are great (day) to good (night). I can zoom in with the app and check on a few specific items of interest. Note: make sure to set passwords into your cameras so not everyone can access them. All of my cameras are exterior. Personally, I will not put a camera inside in case someone does "hack" into my video stream. It is not good to let unsavory people see when you are at home or even what you have in your home (that tv on the wall sure looks nice.....). That said, the 8-count cameras with the system I purchased do a great job of providing total coverage of the outside of my home. One additional feature is the ability to tie the cameras into my current alarm system. This will be done by my alarm company once I am sure I have my cameras set up so they are not overly sensitive, so as not to set off the alarm needlessly. I also ran the recorder video out to my television so I can quickly see who is approaching my home and at my front door before I open it. This was done via the HDMI output on the recorder (and my wiring abilities). I chose this wired system knowing that many wireless options are available. I believe my comments about setting passwords above should give the reason why I believe wired systems are better (for my application). The electronic manuals (on the cd) are much better than the paper one with the system. The file for the NVR is in RTF format (Rich Text Format), not in a locked PDF (bad form Peter Pan). But the manuals overall are complete and the source of the games listed in my primary review. The software for the cameras leaves a LOT to be desired. The camera viewing they want to limit to Internet Explorer only (via quicktime). I use other browsers, so my experience is somewhat limited. But the IE experience still leaves enough to be desired. Finding the cameras via the browser takes more technical knowledge than most people have. They could improve the browser experience a lot in my humble opinion (IMHO). There is recording/playback software also on the CD. I have YET to get it to set up or work properly. I believe it is designed more for use with cameras which are NOT connected to a recorder, but directly to your network. For that, the application may be acceptable when designating your local computer or network attached storage (NAS). However, I did not get it to even view all of the cameras properly, and the manual, of course, leaves much to be desired. My recommendation is to use the network recorder documentation off of the CD and not hassle with the rest. The recorder is worth the cost paid for it as part of the system. Coupling the network recorder and the XMEye app, I don't need my web browser on my desktop/laptop computer to work what needs worked. The biggest draw-back for the XMEye app is the lack of ability to go back and view the alerts (playback), it only shows live. Let's hope your cell provider and email setup can get you alerts fast enough to see the delivery guy drop off a package or that you are alerted with enough time to see the face of the folks who steal your Christmas lights from your yard. Overall, I have no problem recommending this system to others. If some of my neighbors want help installing it in their homes, I will help there as well. Again, I feel, that for me, and my demands, the 5-star rating is worth it. - K. C.

I would return the leaf but my dog chewed the amplifier cord before I got it boxed back up. I would just replace the cord and return it but a replacement amplifier cord costs $50. We live in Northwest Las Vegas, I know results can vary everywhere, but if you live in this area, don’t bother with the Leaf.

The university I go to has really really tough regulations when it comes to anything connecting to their ethernet ports (which school doesn't?). And I was really worried that this dual band router would have to go through some intense trouble shooting because of our school's anti router-in-the-dorm policy. Certainly not a problem for this guy!! I was so happy when I installed my router and got an immediate connection! It's no Gigabit router, but it's sure faster than the G routers and really makes use of our school's T1 lines. At first I was really hesitant when I read the negative reviews for the refurbished products. Let me just say this... if it says "Cisco Certified Refurbished Product" you really have nothing to worry about. It states clearly that you have a 90-day warranty on top of their certified label. In addition, my router came looking brand new! It didn't even have scuffs or blemishes or any malfunctioning parts. Another plus. So for the sake of first appearances, I was overjoyed to get such a deal. Now onto the mechanics. I do not know how much I can comment on since I am not a techie or know a lot about routers. All I knew was that this router had to bypass concrete walls and have a really strong signal. I did a bit of research into the dual-band properties of this router, and while my iphone doesn't connect at the 5Ghz broadcast, it gets a very strong connection at 2.4Ghz. A lot of equipment at your office/home run on the 2.4Ghz signal and therefore congests the signal between your wifi devices and the router, leading to suffering connection speeds. Your laptops/wifi devices should be able to connect to the 5Ghz and get a much stronger and solid connection at this level with your router. Really nice in my opinion. My mac also had no problems recognizing and installing the program that came with it. (Yes, download the driver off of cisco's website!!!) Here is what you have to keep in mind fellow mac users: 1) DOWNLOAD THE DRIVER/PROGRAM from cisco's website!!! I can't stress this enough. You will save yourself a lot of work trying to do common things if you just install this crucial program. If you use the *install disc* that came with it, know that OSX Lion will not be supported and it will say not compatible (hence the online download I mentioned). So go online and install the program.I don't like doing the whole "type in your router/ip address" thing. A lot of users like this because you can do all of the things from the program and a lot more advanced options on the web browser, but if you aren't technical like me and appreciate everything being nice and neat and organized, go with the program you downloaded. Plus, there is a link on the program that takes you to the webpage with your router's information where you can adjust more advanced options. So its better to install the program anyway. The only time where you cannot avoid using the webpage to adjust your router is installing firmware updates. I don't believe this router is self-upgradeable, so you would have to check up on cisco's website for the newest firmware updates as they come. Firmware updates aren't critical per-say....but if you are paranoid about security like me, I would advise you to check the website for firmware updates at least once a month. 2) Don't get frustrated with the loading/installing time. You install the program first into your mac and THEN power the router and connect it to the MODEM! (refer to the instructions the program guides you through). The program will take quite some time to do the necessary installation and setup of your router. Just don't do anything that will interfere with the process (ie. restarting the program, shutting off the router, connecting devices into the router during setup, etc.). Just focus on getting it set up. But just know that even changing the name and password of your router as it appears on wifi connections does take some time too. But once it completes the task, the change is immediate and you're ready to go. 3) I would immediately shut off the guest access (via the program installed) once you have this router up and running. It not only keeps others from clogging up your connection, but it also disables their ability to connect to your highly sought after 5Ghz broadcast as well. The program (aside from the loading times) was really easy and enjoyable to use. I have changed my router name and password over 10 times just for the heck of it and have not had to restart the router for any reason. It is simple and easy to do. There are even "keys" you can make on a usb drive to connect your other wifi devices to the router. Not mind-blowing, but kinda cool. Seems very well ventilated. It has a little foot on the edge that prevents you from placing anything on top of the router, but it allows for airflow on the bottom as well as the sides. So far a pretty solid router and a really valuable amenity for any college dorm (5Ghz is a life saver- like driving in carpool). The customer service is extremely slow however and I'd say moderately informed staff? They prefer online chat to solve your troubles more than any other method. Oh well, at least they helped guide me through installing the latest firmware. Happy Hunting! *****update****** November 7, 2012 The router is still going strong. Had a couple of road blocks: switching dorms for the next year and our school's FiberOptic Line upgrade. Both obstacles did not hinder this router and my mac (OSX LION) is still performing flawlessly with the router. Recently opened up some new ports and got a VPN and completely bypassing the school's throttling. To add somethiing else cool, the range on this baby is sweet. We have a coffee shop 3 floors below us. I still get wifi connection on my iphone. Pretty flippin' sweet. Again, totally depends where your router is setup, etc, etc. But this does not cease to amaze me. By now though there are probably better routers out there for the same price. Make sure you get a router that has AOSS or wifi protected setup button. Things like setting up a wireless printer can be such a pain without that function. Also! Had a wifi enabled brother printer in my room which was a pain to try and manually connect. There is this blue button on the back of the router which basically tells the router to "look for potential wifi devices" (ie. my brother printer) and in less than 2 minutes, I had set up wireless printing in my room! This thing is amazing and I think it's one of my best purchases. *****update***** May 17, 2013 Since updating to OSX Mountain Lion, I can no longer use the downloaded program. I cannot open it, make router changes, or change my password. I do not know why...this isn't a power pc program because it worked well with OSX Lion. So to repeat, on the Cisco site, there is NO UPDATE available for the Linksys E2500. For few select routers, there is an update that you can download on the site for OSX Mountain Lion. But NONE for this router. :( I still get connection, but it stinks to not have this program functionality. Just letting others know!

Just received the unit today. The unit is nice-looking but that's about it. The electronic design is very poor: 1. CURRENT DISPLAY. Shows ZERO on the Amperes display if there is no load even while turning the current limit knob. This means you cannot set the current limit prior to connecting the load. This can be a problem in several situations such as dynamically changing loads (e.g. while testing thermoelectric Peltier modules where a precise amount of electrical energy needs to be applied and measured). 2. CURRENT LIMITING. The voltage starts cycling ON-OFF like a square wave if the load draws more than the set current. This is NOT how constant-current supplies are supposed to work. A properly designed supply should lower the voltage and maintain the set current. FAULTY design!! The above two are ABSOLUTELY unacceptable. The following are livable but still poor design performance: 3. VOLTAGE DISPLAY. At least the voltage display should have had 1 more digits to the right of the decimal (i.e. 10mV) since the voltage knob is multi-turn and this level of voltage adjustment is sometimes needed especially if they are calling this a "Lab Power supply". 4. CURRENT KNOB. The current set knob is a single turn (turns about 270 degrees only) pot. For a 30A supply that I got, they should have also made this multi-turn as it is very difficult to accurately set it to say 7.2A 5. VOLTAGE CHANGE. With no load or light load, reducing the voltage by using the knob reduces the voltage very slowly (can take several seconds to come down). That's because they have a large output capacitor that they are not discharging rapidly using additional electronics (to save cost?) UPDATE (Feb 11, 2020): 6. ROUNDING. A 12.39V reads as 12.3V. Same with current. 7. NO REVERSE POLARITY PROTECTION. This is important if you are going to charge a battery.

My grandfather once told me that all cheeses were made in the same factory so it doesn't matter which cheddar, for example, you purchase. This isn't literally true, of course, but the point he was trying to make is that something that costs more isn't always better than a cheaper version of the same thing. With his voice in mind I purchased both the Polaroid [[ASIN:B009DMJWDC Polaroid Canon EOS Macro Extension Tube Set For Extreme Close Up Photography]] AND the [[ASIN:B0000DZ5OE Canon EF 12 II Extension Tube For EOS Digital Cameras]] and put them to the test to see which was the greater value. Here are my findings: 1. I'm happy that I bought both. 2. They decidedly do not represent different price points of the same thing. The fact that I originally thought they did only reflects my growing, yet still weak, expertise in the paraphernalia of macro photography. 3. The Polaroid tube is made up of 7mm, 14mm, and 28mm lengths that can be used individually or in any combination. 4. The Polaroid tube is just that...a tube, and supports no electronic connection between camera body and lens. In my book this is absolutely fine as long as what you are photographing is not moving and you have the time to make the necessary positional, exposure, and lighting corrections. Photographing jewelry in a static and controlled environment would be a good example. 5. The Canon tube, more like a thick ring actually (The [[ASIN:B0000U1N38 Canon EF 25 II Extension Tube for EOS Digital Cameras]] is a bit more tube-like.) is of a single fixed 12mm length and supports complete connectivity between camera and lens so that exposure and focusing are done as seamlessly with the EF 12 as without. This is a huge benefit if what you are trying to photograph is in a changing environment or moving. Macro photos of insects comes to mind. Yes, I actually did this while building lesson plans for my Biology class. So, while my experiment to determine relative value was a bit misguided, I did end up with two devices I use frequently and would be unhappy to part with. As I said, they are not 'of a kind' and have separate yet strong appeal. If the Canon tube is a cheese it would be a fine Brillat-Savarin while the Polaroid isn't a cheese at all, but a really nice set of pliers.

I bought a Dell XPS 8900 PC back in 2017. On the Boot Menu (press and preferably hold F2 when you turn the PC on) I found out the memory specs: Memory Installed: 16384 MB [or 16 GB] Speed: 2133 MHz Channel Mode: Dual Technology: DDR4 SDRAM DIMM 1 Size: 8192 MB [or 8 GB] DIMM 2 Size: 8192 MB [or 8 GB] DIMM 3 Size: Empty DIMM 4 Size: Empty So I bought two A-Tech 8GB DDR4 2133MHz DIMM PC4-17000 UDIMM Non-ECC 1.2V CL15 288-Pin Desktop Computer RAM Memory Upgrade Modules. Installation was a breeze and they worked. The PC recognized them readily. I was worried by the "UDIMM" term, but on a cursory lookup on Google, it seems that DIMM and UDIMM are the same thing (unregistered memory). I was also worried by the "PC4-17000" term, so I looked it up and found it refers to the DDR4 speed. DDR4 Speeds: PC4-21300 (2666MHz) - PC4-22400 (2800MHz) - PC4-19200 (2400MHz) - PC4-24000 (3000MHz) PC4-17000 (2133MHz) - PC4-25600 (3200MHz) - PC4-26400 (3300MHz) Bottom line, if your PC is a Dell XPS 8900 with 16 GB RAM, chances are this item is what you need to fill'er up to 32 GB (2 x 8GB memory modules).

Where do I start.. The good: picture quality is good. Both day and night. With the spotlight, night vision is great but you don't get much distance. Very little lag time when live streaming to your phone. That's it. The bad: Motion detection. The camera only records when motion is detected. Problem lies when the motion it detects is literally only the traffic driving by. And even that is spuratic at best. I can walk into the driveway, open the door to my truck, drop the tailgate, unload the tools, get back in the truck and drive away with no detection at all. The the neighbor drives by on his way home and motion detected. I tried with and without zones. People only or all motion. It just doesn't matter. I played with sensitivity. It just is so spuratic. Almost never did it record me getting into my truck but occasionally picked up my truck as the tail lights pull out of the driveway. Usually it would detect a person if a dog was there but not if a person didn't have a dog. It missed the FedEx guy dropping a package at my door. Then it missed me taking the package. Then it got the solicitor selling solar panels but not until I opened the front door. Battery.. I understand that when it detects the cars driving by the battery won't give you 6 months but I only got 4 days on one camera. The other 3 including one 2 pro add on with 360 day battery were down to 3 out of 4 bars after just 10 days so the math says maybe a month would be expected. Then there's the footage. On the setting it was on it should have recorded for 1 minute every time an event was detected. Instead I got anywhere from 7 seconds to 24 seconds with one 58 second recording when absolutely nothing was there. I had high hopes and it just didn't pan out.

After realizing that Airport Extreme hasn’t had an update in 3 years and they were not WiFi 6 while all of our Apple Devices are WiFi 6 capable, I started to research various Routers with WiFi 6 capabilities. My final solution in our 2 story 3,300 sq. foot house consists of the following TP-Link AX1800 Router TP-Link RE700X Range Extender TP-Link RE600X Range Extender The areas with the dead spots are completely covered and speed test regularly between 90Mbps down/up. The furthest point of the house now test regularly over 150Mbps down and 100 up. The AppleTV in the living room is now using the ethernet connection on the RE700X and works wonderfully. I researched this particular model against the Garmin 660 for a few weeks, and I finally settled on buying the Magellan 4050 instead. I'm glad I did. I have used a Magellan roadmate 300 in my personal car for years, but the map was old, and there were no free updates for it. I own stock in Garmin, and the company has done well, so I had figured for years that I would buy a Garmin when I was ready to replace my roadmate. I travel quite a bit, and I always rent the navigation system when I rent cars. I have used Garmin quite a bit in that context, and I have always been frustrated by the fact that Garmin units do do not tell the driver which direction their upcoming turn is going to be. Sounds simple enough, and I always figured that the rental car models were just using an old version of Garmin software, and the newer Garmin models would have solved this problem. After reviewing the latest Garmin software, I see the problem still exists where they do not tell the driver the direction of the upcoming turn. I contacted Garmin, and was told they do tell the direction, but they only say it in terms of "North, South, Northwest, etc ..." In other words, "Turn Northwest of [upcoming road]" is printed on the screen. That just wasn't good enough for me, as I just don't know north-south-east-west well enough, so I like it to print "left or right", and that is exactly what Magellan does - in addition, Magellan goes into a split-screen display before the turn, and shows the drive the exact drawing of the turn, so if its not a 90 degree turn, the drive will know what to expect before they get to it. No surprises here, and no accidentally being in the wrong lane when the turn comes up either, which has bit me a few times when using Garmin. That is a feature I have grown to love, and the Magellan having it, and being the cheaper model of the two units really is what made the choice simple for me. My recommendation is to buy the Magellan GPS, and use the money you save to buy some Garmin stock :) Also, I have had no problems with the unit, it feels solid, and is much faster than my old Roadmate unit was. I am not disappointed in my decision to purchase this unit at all.

I will follow this up with a video of the weather radio weekly test when I have the time to trim the video file down in size. The weather station: (See update at bottom of review) - It took me some time to figure out where to mount the outdoor sensor for this unit, it is quite sensitive (as it should be I suppose) ... I finally mounted this under my deck, in a hanging configuration. This keeps the sensor out of sunlight and does not allow the temperature of the mounting platform to impact the readings, it has provided me with very accurate temperature and humidity readings. - Please see update below for rest of weather station notes (initial review was posted before I could properly review the weather portion of this device) ------------------ The weather radio ------------------ PROs: - Radio uses SAME codes to limit the alerts that you will receive to only the counties you want to hear alerts for. - I was able to witness the radio activate for the weekly test today when I was home sick from work - Radio emitted a loud tone prior to the test message, the tone is loud enough to wake you if it is in the same room as you - Tone ended with enough time to hear the entire test message - The radio recognized the end of alert signals and turned itself back off when the alert was complete. Some radio's do NOT do this and instead operate on a timer, this is an issue for two reasons: - It's annoying to continue hearing broadcasts in the middle of the night if the alert is not something you want to wake for - Sometimes messages can take more time than the radio's remain on for (i.e. warnings that cover many counties) - As stated above, this radio does not have these issues. - The radio remained in the "Advisory" status until the alert end time was reached, the radio itself does not continue to talk but it still has the "Advisory" light and continues to scroll what the alert is on the screen (i.e. Required monthly test until 1119am) until the end time. - Is portable, very easy to carry around with you if needed --- Runs on standard AA batteries (3) . I am using Eneloop cells in the radio as I tend to carry it around with me if I am out and about on bad weather days. Batteries will last a few days of use (listening to the weather on occasion, in standby most of the time). Note that the radio does not charge batteries when in the dock, it just does not use battery power when docked. - You can select which alerts you want to hear, with the exception of WARNINGs... There is no way to turn off warnings on this radio (I believe they are not allowed to have this functionality) CONs: - My belt clip broke after only 2 battery changes, the latch is quite weak and it no longer latches into the radio ... This is not a huge issue for me, but could be for some - When changing the batteries the radio will loose some of it's settings, it remembers FIPS (SAME) codes, however you will have to reset the time and date any time you change the batteries. The time and date is important for the automated warning functions in the radio. Other notes: - The radio will keep the past 4 alerts in memory until they expire, after that it reverts to "NO MESSAGE"... The weekly test is NOT stored in memory, so the only way to really determine if the radio is working properly is to be around when the weekly test takes place, or get an actual alert. -------------------- Update 4/27/12: - The weather station has completed learning. During the learning process, I was concerned because pressure was showing way off, and the forcast had become very unpredictable after writing the original review. I checked everything today against the weather radio announcements and found that temp and humidity were 100% perfect, those are VERY accurate. The pressure is also showing accurate, my reading is only .03 off of what the weather radio announces, which is probably correct due to slight difference in elevation. During the training process it was showing over .5 off which was very significant, so don't be surprised if you see numbers that are way off during the first 2 weeks of operation. - Overall I am very impressed that this device "trained" itself properly, I am very impressed by the accuracy of all of the readings, and so far the "forcast" function is not doing too bad (I would not expect any better from a single sensor forcast unit). - Be very careful where you mount the sensor! It took me a few tries to find a spot that did not give false readings due to sunlight, heated surfaces, etc. - I consider this a good deal. 5 stars on the weather station, 4 stars for the radio. ==== Update May 01 2012 ==== Today was a busy day of weather alerts. I noticed something about the radio today, if the radio receives a new alert it will no longer default to displaying an earlier alert if the new one cancels first. In today's example, the radio received a Tornado Watch that was valid until 10pm, it then received 3 Thunderstorm Warnings which all expired by 8pm, once the last thunderstorm warning expired, the radio no longer shows that there is still a tornado watch in effect. I expected that it would revert back to the "Watch" mode with the remaining alert being displayed, however it did not, even though the Tornado Watch is still in the "History" of the unit (It holds the last 4 non-expired alerts). I view this as an oversight in the design of the radio. I still personally rate this entire setup at 4 stars and will not be taking another star off, the radio still performs and will alert you to the current weather events taking place which is the most important function of the radio.

I just bought a Wyze Security Camera, and I bought this 255 Watt UPS to keep the camera going during power outages. I repeated this test just to be sure. This feature is important to me since I'm using the camera in a vacation home, and no one will be there to reset the UPS or the camera if the power goes out. I purchased this DVD player in order to replace an old, dead DVD player and to play DivX/Xvid on my TV. It has so far performed as expected. A few minor complaints: 1. There does not appear to be any way to get back to the DivX/Xvid file menu once you start one playing. Somewhat annoying. 2. The DVD tray is incredibly thin... about as thin as a DVD. So you have to be a bit careful when putting the disc in. I just doesn't ever feel like it's on the tray properly. 3. If your DivX/Xvid file has any errors it will not play. There were files that played fine on my computer, but the DVD player just couldn't handle the error. There are free tools to fix problems in DivX/Xvid files which I had to use on a few files to get them to play. Otherwise it plays DVDs fine, plays DivX/Xvid fine and overall seems to be a perfectly reasonable player for a good price.

Tldr: There was tape with a strong adhesive on the SURFACE of the TV screen along the edge. I know TVs usually have plastic along the bezel that needs to be removed after set up. This is different. This may as well be packing tape, adhered strongly directly to the screen, not the bezel. This does not appear to be an anomaly either as the expected bezel wrap was there as well. It seems the tape was added along the center of each side. When I worked Help Desk I had unboxed configured and wall mounted several dozen TVs. This seems like kind of a weird thing to have an efficient understanding in but basic TV set up is something I am an actual professional of. This is by far the worst and most destructive packaging I've ever seen. Even after running the TV for a bit to soften the adhesive, and carefully and slowly removing the tape, the pell from the adhesive was incredibly and permanently damaging to the screen. I am most advising not to purchase this TV, but I'd you do purchase it and see the tape, IMMEDIATELY rebox it and demand a full refund. Removing the tape WILL damage the TV.
